stem: A company runs an order API on Amazon API Gateway. The API invokes an AWS Lambda function that writes each order to a small Amazon RDS for MySQL database. During traffic spikes, so many copies of the function connect at the same time that the database fails. The function must never run more than 50 copies at the same time. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?
keywords: The function must never run more than 50 copies at the same time

options.text: Set the reserved concurrency of the function to 50, and keep the API Gateway integration pointed at the function as it is today.
options.why: Reserved concurrency can [cap traffic rates to downstream resources](../facts/lambda.md#lambda-faq-per-function-concurrency-control), so Lambda runs 50 copies or fewer and throttles the rest.

options.text: Configure provisioned concurrency of 50 on a published alias of the function, and point the API Gateway integration at that alias.
options.why: Provisioned concurrency is no ceiling, because Lambda can scale the function [above and beyond your provisioned concurrency setting](../facts/lambda.md#lambda-pc-scales-beyond-setting).

options.text: Place an Amazon SQS queue between API Gateway and the function, and set the maximum concurrency of the event source mapping to 50.
options.why: It also limits the copies, but a queue, a new integration and an event source mapping are more to build and run than one function setting.

options.text: Move the code into containers on AWS Fargate behind an Application Load Balancer, with an Amazon ECS service whose tasks keep running between requests.
options.why: It moves the whole API to containers, which is far more work, and tasks that keep running set no limit on the copies that connect.
options.misconception: rebuilds the platform to solve a limit that one function setting solves

explanation: The database fails because too many copies connect at once, so the fix is a ceiling on one function. AWS says to configure reserved concurrency to [limit how high your function can scale](../facts/lambda.md#lambda-bp-reserved-protects-downstream). Lambda throttles the requests above the ceiling, and the setting [incurs no additional charges](../facts/lambda.md#lambda-reserved-concurrency-no-charge).
takeaway: Reserved concurrency caps one function, and provisioned concurrency prepares environments without a cap.
twin: If the stem said "After quiet periods, the first requests take several seconds" instead: provisioned concurrency on an alias, because it keeps functions [ready to respond in double-digit milliseconds](../facts/lambda.md#lambda-snapstart-vs-pc-guide).
say: I'd set reserved concurrency to fifty, because it caps the function, so the database never sees more than fifty copies.
